subject: specifying both brow and ncol in facet_wrap

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: specifying both brow and ncol in facet_wrap
parts:
Hi all


In earlier versions of ggplot2 it was possible to specify both ncol and nrow in facet_wrap at the same time. If the number of faceting levels were lower than ncol*nrow the resulting plot would just leave the rest of the plotting areas empty. This was useful for multipage plots where the last page might contain less panels than the rest but maintain the size of the individual panels.

This behavior has changed so that now ggplot2 forces one of either ncol or brow down to a value where the plotarea is almost filled out.


For instance the following

data <- data.frame(a=1:10, b=1:10, c=rep(c('a','b','c','d','e'), each=2))
qplot(data=data, x=a, y=b, geom='point') + facet_wrap(~c, ncol=4, nrow=5, shrink=F)

creates a panel layout equivalent to ncol=4, nrow=2 instead of the one specified.

Is this change intentional and if so is it possible to have a switch to in facet_wrap to avoid it?

best wishes

Thomas

messages.subject: Re: specifying both brow and ncol in facet_wrap
parts:
Now at closer inspection it seems I have fooled myself as this behavior apparently never existed... Sorry about that...

So instead I would like to make this into a feature request. The functionality at the moment is already covered by only specifying either nrow or ncol and letting ggplot2 figure out the missing one. Thus a consistent behavior when specifying both would not remove any functionality.

best wishes

Thomas
